entries.title: Born in Texas.
entries.body: Yeehaw.

entries.title: Moved to Germany.
entries.body: Wore felt hats.

entries.title: Then the UK.
entries.body: Picked up a real-deal posh accent.

entries.title: Belgium.
entries.body: Lost the accent. Still miss the waffles.

entries.title: Back to the US.
entries.body: Suburbs of Cincinnati until college.

entries.title: Messing with computers.
entries.body: Started messing with computers through sketchy Windows XP theme packs and Deus Ex mods.

entries.title: Sociology at Wooster
entries.body: A B.A. at The College of Wooster. A phenomenal statistics professor, Dr. Ann Nurse, got me excited about statistics—and pretty good at it. My senior thesis explored smartphones, identity, and social life, written publicly on GitHub.

entries.title: Dad’s Raleigh.
entries.body: Fixed up an 80's steel frame, mint-green paint and all. Learned how to mechanic some with the campus bike co-op.

entries.title: My first proper road bike.
entries.body: A Fuji Roubaix. I was putting out so much power I nearly tore a chainstay apart and had to warranty the frame. Sold the replacement.

entries.title: Landscape architecture & web design.
entries.body: Working as a landscape architect and designing and building websites.

entries.title: The Hill and Dale Hundred.
entries.body: Rode my uncle’s Gary Fisher mountain bike for Swallow Bicycle Works’ metric century: nearly 7,000 feet of climbing. A choice only a twenty-something could make.

entries.title: Steel is real.
entries.body: An All-City Mr. Pink build by Swallow Bicycle Works. Still have that bike.

entries.title: Building my own corner of the web.
entries.body: My personal site became an important place to learn by building. Kirby in 2014, then DumDum and daisy in 2015: experiments with Meteor, publishing, feeds, and bringing different kinds of posts together. Later came Hexo, and eventually Nuxt. The site kept changing as I did.

entries.title: Global Cloud / DonorDrive.
entries.body: An internship, followed by my first full-time job in data and analytics. I remember the role as Data and Analytics Specialist; exact title and dates still to confirm.

entries.title: JavaScript, R & SQL.
entries.body: Started seriously messing with JavaScript, R, and SQL for the first time after joining Global Cloud.

entries.title: Google Analytics in VR.
entries.body: GAframe: pulling live Google Analytics data into A-Frame, with React components and animated bars. An experiment in taking a dashboard somewhere stranger.

entries.title: Business Analytics at Cincinnati
entries.body: An M.S. in Business Analytics at the University of Cincinnati. My mapping capstone applied districting analysis to Cincinnati police districts, using evolutionary algorithms and R.

entries.title: My first PC build. And CUDA.
entries.body: Built my first PC and started experimenting with CUDA and machine learning. Thought I was hot shit for having a remote server I could run ML jobs on.

entries.title: My first live coding demo.
entries.body: My first live coding demo, with Tim Wilson at MeasureCamp Cincinnati just before officially graduating from UC. We pulled data from the Google Analytics Reporting API to analyze together.

entries.title: Clearhead / Accenture.
entries.body: Senior Data Scientist. Building experimentation programs and working on retention and personalization.

entries.title: surefoot.
entries.body: Digital Analytics Manager. E-commerce experiments, analyst mentorship, and tools to make the work less manual.

entries.title: SoundBlasterBlaster.
entries.body: The culmination of the farewell soundboards: a little Vue soundboard generator to leave behind some of the shenanigans from team calls. Also an excuse to get back into writing code.

entries.title: mhm.social
entries.body: Building and maintaining a small Vue profile site. Its Twitter link becomes a Bluesky link in November 2023.

entries.title: Search Discovery.
entries.body: Senior Optimization Manager. Geographic experiments, causal inference, and teaching experimental methods.

entries.title: The Super Profesh.
entries.body: Bought an All-City Super Professional from Cycle Smithy in Chicago. Tried flat-bar life and hated it.

entries.title: St. Jude / ALSAC.
entries.body: Digital Experimentation Strategist. Working on donation experiences and helping teams build an experimentation practice.

entries.title: Back on the Mr. Pink.
entries.body: The Super Profesh was stolen. Back to the Mr. Pink until the next bike arrived.

entries.title: A personal experiment-tool project.
entries.body: After years of building analysis tools at work, started a personal project for managing and analyzing A/B tests. It would eventually mutate into AlphaBeta.

entries.title: My first LLM conversation.
entries.body: Used an LLM for the first time: Claude, for code review.

entries.title: AlphaBeta changes shape.
entries.body: An A/B analysis tool becomes a broader project about experimental decisions and process.

entries.title: Plinth Board.
entries.body: A visual planning board connecting high-level goals to problems, initiatives, and work items. Built with React, with drag-to-connect cards, multiple planning frameworks, and PDF export.

entries.title: The Disc Trucker arrives.
entries.body: A Surly Disc Trucker from Peregrine Bicycle Studio in Chicago. Ordered it in the spring, then conveniently cracked my kneecap in half.

entries.title: behold.
entries.body: Spinning 3D models in the terminal as characters, blocks, or pixels. A single Python script with no dependencies. Just for the fun of it.

entries.title: Causal inference in a browser.
entries.body: CausalImpact WASM starts as a one-day build. A planning mode and the project’s first external contribution follow in September.
